full_judgment:
Muhammad Ansar Ali, J.: This Second Miscellaneous Appeal under Order XLIII, Rule 1 (U) read with Section 104 of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the Defendants 1-9 is directed against the Judgment and order dated 30.5.85 passed in Title Appeal No. 79 of 1984 by the learned District Judge, Munshigonj, allowing the appeal, setting aside the Judgment and Decree dated 5.2.1984 in Title Suit No. 34 of 1983, passed by the learned Munsif, 4th Court, Munshiganj, and sending the said suit back on remand to the trial Court for fresh hearing and disposal on proper discussion of the evidence or further evidence on record. 

 5) Whether the Plaintiffs are entitled to any decree as prayed for? 

 4. Both the parties examined 6 witnesses from each side and submitted some documents to substantiate their respective claims. The learned Munsif, after hearing the parties and on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, held, with regard to the first issue, that the suit was not maintainable for want of payment of advalorem Court Fees when there was a prayer for consequential relief for injunction apart from the prayer for declaration of title in the suit land. With regard to the issue No. 2, the learned Munsif found from the consideration of the materials on record that the alleged owner of the suit-land, Nirmal Chandra Das, is a factious person and the alleged deed of purchase in his favour is false and fraudulent and his possession in the suit-land is also imaginary. With regard to the 3rd issue, the trial Court came to a finding that the Plaintiffs were not legally appointed Attorneys and they have no actual possession in the suit lands. It is rather the Defendants who have right, title and possession in the suit-lands on the basis of Exts. A-P. With regard to the rest issues the trial Court found that the Plaintiffs are not entitled to any decree or any relief as prayed for and, on consideration of the materials on record, the learned Munsif dismissed the suit on contest as against Defendant, Nos. 1. 2-6 with costs and experte against the rest without cost vide his Judgment and Decree dated 5.2.84. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid Judgment and decree of the learned Munsif, the Plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 79 of 1984 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Munshigonj. The said appeal was contested by the Defendants. The appeal was heard on both the sides. Thereafter, the learned District Judge framed the following point for determination: namely, whether the learned Munsif was justified for dismissing the Plaintiffs-Appellants suit. At the time of hearing of the appeal, the Plaintiff-Appellants, however, filed an application for remanding the suit to the trial Court for fresh decision and the learned District Judge, without going into the evidence on record and discussing the respective claims of the parties to the suit land, allowed the Plaintiffs, prayer for remand of the suit with the following observation: 

 Accordingly, the learned District Judge allowed the appeal against the Respondents without costs, set aside the Judgment and Decree of the trial Court and sent back the suit on remand for hearing in the light of the observation made above and for writing the Judgment according to law after giving the parties a chance to adduce more evidence, both oral and documentary, by calling the originals legally called for, by his Judgment and order dated 30.5.85. The Defendants Respondents of the Court below being aggrieved by the aforesaid Judgment and order of the learned District Judge have preferred the present Miscellaneous Appeal against the impugned order of remand as stated above. 

 5. Mr. Santi Ranjan Karmakar with Mr. L. Gomez, the learned Advocates, appeared for the Defendants-appellants,. From the record, it appears that one Mr. M. A. Jalil, Advocate filed power for the Plaintiff-Respondents 1, 2 and 3 in this appeal, but he has not appeared to contest this appeal on behalf of his clients, though it was kept part heard for a few days. Mr. Karmakar, the learned Advocate, has taken me through both the Judgments of the Courts below and then he has seriously contended, referring to the observation of the learned District Judge, as has been quoted above, that the impugned Judgment and order of remand is wholly had, illegal and is not warranted at all, either under Rule 23, Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure or under Section 151 of the said Code. Referring to the impugned Judgment and order of the learned District Judge, the learned Advocate has contended that the learned District Judge has not discussed the evidence on record as laid by both the parties. Before passing the impugned order of remand, he has not come to any finding as to whether the trial Court had disposed of the suit on a preliminary point and the Decree was liable to be reversed in the appeal or that any important issue or issues were left out and were not considered by the trial Court or that a remand of the suit to the trial Court was necessary for the ends of justice. Rather, it appears that the learned District Judge felt the necessity of sending the suit back on remand to the trial Court only because there was no proper discussing of the evidence on record of the Defendants with regard to their claim of title and possession in the suit-land vis-a-vis the claim of the Plaintiffs and some original documents were required to be produced.
